Who Took the Cake? Rules

A detective puzzle with a friendly case: one of the animals took the cake, and the clues tell you which one.

The rules

The floor plan
The board is a floor plan of squares. Thick lines split it into rooms: Easy has 5x5 squares and 3 rooms, Medium 6x6 and 4 rooms, Hard 7x7 and 5 rooms. Every room has a number in one of its squares; the line under the board says which room it is.
What you place
The cake already lies on the floor plan when the puzzle starts, in any room. You place only the animals (dog, cat, rabbit, mouse and hedgehog, as many as there are rooms): exactly one in every room, never on the cake's square.
Never side by side
Two animals never stand directly next to each other: not side by side, not one above the other and not diagonally - not even with a wall between them.
The clues
The clues below the board say how big an animal's room is (“The dog is in a room with 5 squares”), who stands higher up or further left than whom (in a higher row or a column further left, not necessarily right beside), whose rooms share a wall, and how many steps an animal is away from the cake. Steps go up, down, left or right, never diagonally, and walls do not matter. Together the clues leave only one way to place everything, and you never need to guess.
Who took the cake?
Exactly one animal stands directly next to the cake - beside it, above, below or diagonally, even across a wall. That animal took it.
Playing
Choose a button below the board - an animal, or X for “nothing here” - then tap a cell. Tapping the same cell again with the same choice takes it off. The cake's square cannot be changed. Tap a clue to tick it off. The Hint button points out a mistake first; otherwise it places the animal that can be worked out next and says why.
Levels
Easy: 5x5 with 3 animals and two extra clues; every step follows from one clue or one rule. Medium: 6x6 with 4 animals; you combine clues about two animals. Hard: 7x7 with 5 animals; sometimes you have to think ahead: if an animal stood here, would the others still have a place?
Theme
With the theme “Cats and fish” all the suspects are cats, told apart by their names and patterns: Tiger (striped), Luna (all black), Mimi (white with a bow), Felix (black patches) and Max (collar with a bell). They are after a fish instead of the cake. Everything else - the rules, the clues and the levels - stays the same.
Three more themes work the same way: “Who nibbled the cookies?” with the bears Bruno (bow tie), Paula (all black), Otto (glasses), Lilli (flower) and Fritz (woolly hat); “Who hid the ball?” with the dogs Bello (spots), Lotte (all black), Benny (eye patch), Susi (bow) and Rudi (neckerchief); and “Who mislaid the key?” with the magpies Pip (crest), Kiki (glasses), Rosa (bow), Jakob (top hat) and Lou (scarf).
Two themes have people as suspects: “Who took the cake?” with the family Greta (bun and glasses), Anton (beard), Lisa (long hair), Jonas (tie) and Emma (pigtails); and “Who hid the treasure?” with the neighbours' children Tom (cap), Nora (bow), Ben (curls), Ida (sun hat) and Leo (spiky hair), who look for a chest of gold coins. Two people never stand directly next to each other; everything else stays the same.

How to go about it

  1. Start with the room sizes and the steps to the cake: an animal in a room with 3 squares can only be in a room of that size, and an animal 4 steps from the cake only on a square that far away. Mark the squares where it cannot be with X.
  2. Use the rooms: once an animal stands in a room, nobody else goes there, and the squares around it stay free of other animals. If only one animal can still reach a room, it goes there.
  3. Combine clues about two animals: if the dog stands higher up than the cat, the dog is never in the bottom row and the cat never in the top row.
  4. Keep an eye on the cake: exactly one animal stands next to it. If only one animal can still get there, it stands there; once one stands there, the others keep away. Tick off clues you have used. If you get stuck, the Hint button sets the next animal and says why.

A solved example

The picture shows a solved 5x5 puzzle with three rooms. Every room holds one animal, no two animals touch, and the cake touches only the rabbit - so the rabbit took the cake. The dog and the cat stand further away.

Finishing a puzzle

Solved
The puzzle is solved as soon as every animal stands in its right place. The message then names the animal next to the cake: it took the cake.
